bull_bear.body:
- **Debt-free; ₹1,308cr cash.** Self-funds R&D (key differentiator vs DRDO-co-funded peers).
- **M&A active:** scouting acquisitions in simulators, anti-drone, and "Pareto technologies" (20% of tech that decides 80% of war); model = supply capital + ecosystem guidance to focused small companies.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Order-timing risk:** FY27 is heavily back-end-loaded (Q2–Q3 execution); any slip on the awaited Q1/Q2 inflows dents the ₹4,000cr cumulative target.
- **Policy risk:** draft DAP language equating ToT/foreign-IP "made in India" with IDDM could blunt the self-funded innovator's edge — mgmt lobbying against it.
- **Foreign-procurement pull:** armed-forces preference for ready foreign "patch-up" buys in the near term (mgmt downplays it strongly).
- **Frequency "catch-up game":** adversary drones shifting bands (10 MHz–12 GHz) force constant counter-drone R&D — structurally elevated R&D cost base.
- Ammunition certification complexity ("two-year period should be sufficient").
- Lumpy, government-dependent ordering; elevated working capital during execution years.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Highly confident, mission-driven, candid on the trough quarter and one-offs. Ashok Atluri visionary/colourful (Godfather, Pareto-recursion, "make Shahed into Shaheed"); CFO precise and numbers-grounded. Strong skin-in-the-game (self-funded R&D, debt-free). Tone: FY26 a deliberate dip, FY27 the inflection; 2026 framed as a "hallmark year" for indigenous IDDM innovators.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The revenue collapse is a feature, not a bug:** Operation Sindoor *pulled forward* emergency anti-drone orders while *pushing out* regular simulator orders — so the ₹1,336cr book + accelerating pipeline matters far more than the -45% Q4.
- **Business-model pivot to "facilitator":** Zen increasingly orchestrates an ecosystem (ARI/UTS/AI-Turing/Vector Technics) rather than building everything itself — AI-driven productivity freed the bandwidth for the product wave.
- **Interceptor-drone economics** ($10k kill of $30k Shahed) directly attack the "$3m missile vs $30k drone" cost-inversion problem — potentially the single biggest future product and a global export story.
- Hard-kill + ammunition + arms licences shift Zen up the kill-chain from detect/jam into the actual neutralization hardware (RCWS, 30mm smart ammo, CIWS) — higher-value, stickier.
- DSO improved 42 days even in a weak revenue quarter — collections quality intact.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Management calls out "the contribution from our subsidiaries to the consolidated revenue and earnings, validating the capital allocation decisions we have made over years", saying these investments "collectively position Zen to compete across a wider set of opportunities going forward".
- Order book as at 31 March 2026 includes Rs 121.81 Cr relating to subsidiary companies, evidencing the subsidiaries' standalone order contribution.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Owns the intellectual property behind its technologies, built through sustained self-funded research rather than licensed assembly, which aligns it with a procurement framework that rewards indigenously designed, developed and manufactured systems
- 94 patents granted to date and the CII Best Patent Portfolio Award 2025, with ₹139.11 crore invested in R&D over the last five years
- Combat validation: its Counter-UAS system was deployed during Operation Sindoor, detecting up to 100 drone threats at a time with a response time under 0.1 seconds and neutralising hundreds of drones and swarm drones
- Wide-band engineering choice — the Counter-UAS system detects and jams drone data links well beyond the commercial 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands, where conventional solutions struggle
- Breadth across five capabilities — training simulation, counter-drone, automated weapon stations, combat robotics and drones — assembled through acquisitions, associates and partnerships
- Over three decades of operating history with 1,000+ training systems shipped worldwide
- Debt-free balance sheet with cash and bank balances of over ₹1,308 crore and the highest Dun & Bradstreet rating of 5A1, reflecting capacity to handle large government contracts
- Government licence under the Arms Act for manufacture of specified weapon systems, together with an ammunition licence
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Order finalisation and conversion timing — lumpy, milestone-based defence contracts — Management attributes the FY26 revenue moderation to delays in order finalisation, shifting procurement priorities and the milestone-based nature of defence contracts; order conversion timing extended beyond expectations, pushing the bulk of recent orders into FY27. The AR separately flags 'order-book uncertainty': developing bespoke systems without finalised orders can pressure cash flows, mitigated by prioritising milestone-based agreements.
- Customer and activity concentration on a single government buyer base — BRSR reports 100% of turnover from one activity — designing, developing and manufacturing combat training solutions for homeland security and counter-drone technology — sold principally to the Ministry of Defence, allied foreign armed forces, state police, security and paramilitary organisations. Exports contributed only 0.14% of total turnover, so the revenue line is effectively tied to Indian government procurement cycles and budget priorities.
- Procurement structure biased to the lowest bidder — Tender processes often favour the lowest bidder, which may not reflect lifecycle value; the Company responds with cost optimisation and lean manufacturing while delivering the technological value required for mission success.
- Competitive dynamics — aggressive pricing by global players — Global players may use aggressive pricing to secure large contracts; the Company relies on deep product customisation, superior technical performance and long-term service relationships to defend value beyond the initial purchase price.
- Technological obsolescence in a fast-moving capability race — Rapid innovation carries the risk of systems becoming outdated; mitigation is continuous investment in next-generation research, agile development and strategic partnerships. The BRSR frames technological advancement as a material issue whose flip side is loss of competitive advantage.
- Cyber security, data privacy and IP theft — As a defence-sector organisation entrusted with sensitive information, a threat-sensitive environment makes the Company a target for digital incursion and intellectual-property theft; breaches could bring legal repercussions, reputational damage and substantial financial losses. Mitigation is a Cyber Risk Management framework, regular security assessments, strict data-access control and encryption, alongside ISO/IEC 27001 adherence.
- Supply-chain fragility and component shortages — Geopolitical instability and component shortages can delay production, causing higher costs and customer dissatisfaction; mitigation is a resilient, multi-tiered and diverse supplier network, regular risk assessments, contingency planning and real-time monitoring.
- Specialised talent acquisition and retention — Specialised defence-technology talent is in high global demand and high turnover raises recruitment cost and destroys accumulated expertise; the permanent-employee turnover rate was 14.01% in FY 2025-26 (16.96% in FY 2024-25). Mitigation is a mission-driven culture, attractive compensation, clear growth pathways and succession planning.

business.body: Zen Technologies, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Hyderabad, designs, develops and manufactures its own defence technologies and retains ownership of the underlying intellectual property. Its offerings run across three lines: training solutions including live ranges and virtual simulation, counter-drone detection and neutralisation technologies, and advanced military hardware including robotic surveillance systems and remote weapon stations. Customers are the Ministry of Defence and the Indian armed forces, central and state police, paramilitary and security forces, and allied foreign armed forces, with a presence across India, the UAE and the United States.

business.body:
- **Live simulation and training systems:** Armour Combat Training System (Zen ACTS), TACSIM Tactical Engagement Simulator
- **Training solutions and live ranges:** Containerised Tubular Shooting Range (CTSR), Containerised Indoor Shooting Range (CISR), Containerised Small Arms Firing Range (CSAFR), Shoot House, Air-to-Ground Firing Range Scoring System, Smart Target System (Zen STS) with LOMAH, Multi-Functional Target System (MFTS), Tank Targets
- **Virtual simulators:** Tank Driving Simulator (T-90), Tank Crew Gunnery Simulator (T-90), IFV/APC Driving Simulator, Anti-drone simulator
- **Counter-drone / Counter-UAS:** Counter-UAS multi-layer, multi-sensor system, Hawkeye AI-powered multi-sensor camera, VyomKavach hybrid Counter-UAS system
- **Weapon stations and combat robotics:** Barbarik AI-powered Remote Controlled Weapon Station, Parashu AI-powered Remote Controlled Weapon Station, Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle, Hyperstrike loitering strike platform, 30 mm programmable ammunition, Compact gun-and-missile system for naval forces
- **Naval and marine simulation:** Naval tactical trainers, Submarine simulators

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **HyperStrike interceptor/loiter drone** — $10k cost vs $30k Shahed, 400 km/h, 5-min loiter, 20km+ range, AI tracking + manual override, capacity 5,000/shift/month scalable to 15,000; production starts FY27. Mgmt: *"could be the largest product in our portfolio two years out."*
- **Counter-drone hardware:** widened frequency dominance **70 MHz–12 GHz** (vs 400 MHz–6 GHz earlier), 15km+ detection, indigenized 20km radar, RF/GNSS jamming + RCWS/L70/ZU-23 hard-kill.
- **Vrishabh UGV** (combat/logistics/casualty-evac, 150kg payload, 50 km/h, 100km range, >85% indigenous) — commercial launch FY27.
- **30mm smart ammunition** (10×10m kill radius, anti-drone, no weapon modification) — manufacture/supply from FY27.
- **Cybersecurity suite ("Suraksha")** — 6-layer, post-quantum-ready, zero foreign dependency; for command centres/ships/aircraft.
- **Naval simulation** (mine-clearance, choke-point e.g. Hormuz) — full combat naval training centres; export interest via ARI.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build an integrated indigenous defence technology ecosystem — expanding beyond conventional simulation through focused acquisitions, associates and strategic investments across naval simulation, autonomous systems and aerospace technologies.
- Keep design ownership in India: an 'owned-by-India' philosophy that treats product design as a national strategic asset, with research funded from the Company's own resources rather than licensed assembly.
- Offer the armed forces five capabilities — training simulation and systems, counter-drone solutions, automated weapon stations, combat robotics and drones — built through sustained investment and a series of acquisitions and partnerships.
- Stay ahead in counter-drone: widen the frequency coverage of anti-drone systems beyond commercial bands, strengthen neutralisation options across RF and GNSS jamming, weapon stations and air-defence gun integration, and offer an anti-drone simulator for rehearsal against single drones and swarms.
- Expand the innovation footprint to meet demand for autonomous and aerial defence solutions — a new R&D and manufacturing facility is being developed at the Electronic Manufacturing Cluster in Tuem, Goa, alongside continued build-out of software and AI development capability for combat robotics and autonomous systems.
- Deepen naval training capability by combining Anawave with Applied Research International to support an integrated Naval Training Centre, addressing strong overseas demand.
- Develop a defence-grade Cyber Security Suite with subsidiaries — a six-layer integrated solution for command and control centres, ships and aircraft, designed with zero foreign dependencies.
- Act as a platform for indigenous defence technology, bringing together a group of specialist companies and giving them the support to meet the country's requirements.
- Design new platforms such as the Hyperstrike loitering strike platform for scaled production, and address the cost asymmetry where low-cost drones are met only by far more expensive interceptors.
- Establish the environmental case for simulation-based training scientifically through joint studies with TERI covering emissions, the net present value of environmental savings and the single-day cost of non-induction.
- The Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published on its website under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. For FY26 the Board, on May 01, 2026, recommended a final dividend of ₹1 per equity share of ₹1 each (100% of face value), stated to be 'in view of the overall performance of the Company, while retaining capital to support future growth and in line with the Dividend Distribution Policy'; the resolution is placed before the 33rd AGM on August 29, 2026, with a record date of August 21, 2026. No amount was transferred to reserves during the year, and no deposits were accepted from the public. Management describes the balance sheet as strong and debt-free. On related-party dealings, all transactions during the year were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's-length basis, with no materially significant related-party transactions with promoters, directors or KMP that could conflict with the Company's interests; omnibus Audit Committee approval is taken for repetitive transactions (most of which are with subsidiaries) and reviewed quarterly. The Company made no application under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 during FY 2025-26, and maintains a D&O liability insurance policy covering members of the Board and officers.
- BRSR disclosures for FY 2025-26 are made on a standalone basis and carry reasonable assurance on BRSR core indicators from TUV India Private Limited.
- 28.54% of R&D investment in FY 2025-26 (14.2% in FY 2024-25) went into specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impact of products and processes; the equivalent capex share is reported as '-' (not disclosed).
- Product-level environmental design choices disclosed: natural gas compressors instead of CO₂ for weapon recoil to reduce emissions; visuals projected onto walls rather than synthetic materials to cut plastic use; HVAC systems in container shooting ranges that capture smoke; and recovery and reuse of lead from fired bullets.
- Energy and emissions is identified as a material risk in the BRSR materiality table, with the stated response being investment in energy-efficient technologies and renewable-energy integration across manufacturing processes.
- Policies mapped to all nine NGRBC principles are Board-approved and published, including a Business Responsibility Policy, Risk Management Policy, Code of Conduct, Health and Safety Policy, Human Rights Policy, Policy on Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace, Environment Policy and CSR Policy; the policies extend to value-chain partners for all principles except Principle 2.
- Policies are aligned to ISO 9001:2015 for quality management and ISO/IEC 27001:2013 for information security (the MD&A Company Overview cites ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification).
- The ESG framework is externally benchmarked through the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment, which underlies the Dow Jones Sustainability Index.
- Highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the Business Responsibility policies is Mr. Ashok Atluri, Chairman & Managing Director; a Risk Management Committee (chaired by independent director Mr. Sanjay Vijay Singh Jesrani) and a Board-approved Risk Management Policy are in place, with risk procedures reviewed by the Audit Committee and Risk Management Committee.
- Grievance redressal: one shareholder complaint was filed in FY 2025-26 (one in FY 2024-25), resolved and closed, with nil complaints from investors, communities, employees and workers, customers, value-chain partners and others; nil conflict-of-interest complaints in respect of Directors and KMPs.
- The Company commissioned TERI (The Energy and Resources Institute) in March 2023 for a joint study establishing the environmental signatures of its simulators; the first study was launched on World Environment Day, 5 June 2023, and a second, deeper study covering a larger set of simulator types — assessing emissions, the net present value of environmental savings and the single-day cost of non-induction — has been completed and is being prepared for launch.
- The BRSR does not state any quantified, time-bound ESG target: its answer on 'specific commitments, goals and targets set with defined timelines' describes short-, medium- and long-term goal categories in narrative terms only, with no metric, baseline or target date.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is expanding its research footprint to meet demand for autonomous and aerial defence solutions. A new R&D and manufacturing facility is being developed at the Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) in Tuem, Goa — described as an upcoming 'Advanced R&D' facility — while the Company continues to build its software and AI development capability for combat robotics and autonomous systems. Its existing footprint comprises the R&D Centre at Sanath Nagar, Hyderabad (recognised by the Ministry of Science and Technology, and dedicated to next-generation simulation platforms and anti-drone architectures), a Demo Centre cum Factory near Shamshabad Airport that showcases training ecosystems and counter-drone systems to domestic and international clients, and the Software and AI Development Centre at Kondapur, Hyderabad, which supports deep-learning models for the Hawkeye platforms and adaptive-learning models for simulators in secure, air-gapped environments. The Maheshwaram unit in Hyderabad was commissioned in 2009. Capital commitments outstanding at the balance-sheet date relate to construction of a new factory building and others. On the product side, the Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle — 150 kg payload, up to 50 km/h, range up to 100 km, indigenous content above 85% — is planned for commercial launch in FY27, and the Hyperstrike loitering strike platform is designed for scaled production, with its high-speed propulsion system supplied by subsidiary Vector Technics.

outlook.body:
- FY26 revenue moderation was attributed to delays in order finalisation, shifting procurement priorities and the milestone-based nature of defence contracts; order conversion timing extended beyond management's expectations, with the bulk of recent orders scheduled for execution from FY27.
- Management states underlying momentum remained robust across simulation systems, counter-UAS technologies and emerging autonomous platforms.
- Management expects the draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 to compress the procurement cycle considerably and to open new growth opportunities for companies with genuine indigenous capability and intellectual property; it also expects order wins to begin flowing through in the near term.
- DAP 2026 introduces Long-Term Bulk Acquisition, giving industry ten-year visibility on orders, and Low-Cost Capital Acquisition for fast-moving technologies such as drones and artificial intelligence, with emphasis on indigenously designed, developed and manufactured technologies.
- The Union Budget for FY27 carried a record allocation of approximately ₹7.85 lakh crore to the Ministry of Defence, up about 15.19%, with approximately ₹1.85 lakh crore towards capital acquisitions of advanced platforms, weapon systems, drones and counter-drone technologies, and about 75% of the capital acquisition budget earmarked for domestic defence firms.
- India's counter-drone market is projected to grow at a 24.4% compound annual rate to reach US$1.39 billion by 2030.
- Demand for layered anti-drone systems has surged in the wake of regional conflicts, with a shift towards wide-band electronic warfare solutions able to disrupt communication and navigation across non-standard frequencies — the design premise of the Company's own system.
- The military is moving towards Integrated Combat Training Nodes that combine live firing with virtual and constructive simulation, and the Indian Army has declared 2026 the year of Networking and Data Centricity.
- The private sector's contribution to defence production has climbed to 23%, with order books for private firms estimated to reach ₹55,000 crore by the end of FY26.
- Indigenous defence production reached approximately ₹1.54 lakh crore in FY25 with FY26 projected to surpass the ₹1.75 lakh crore target; defence exports reportedly reached an all-time high of approximately ₹38,424 crore in FY26.
- Subsidiaries and associates — Applied Research International, Vector Technics, Bhairav Robotics and AI Turing — added to consolidated revenue and earnings, described by management as validating past capital allocation decisions.
- Results should be read within the context of the defence sector's procurement cycles; the strong FY25 revenue base was driven by concentrated order execution.
- Consolidated order book of ₹1,336.04 crore at the close of FY26 (approximately ₹1,336 crore as at 31 March 2026), described as providing strong revenue visibility.
- Standalone order book stood at ₹1,222.6 crore.
- New order inflows of ₹431.36 crore were secured during the fourth quarter alone.
- The majority of the order book is scheduled for execution from FY27, and about ₹1,000 crore is expected to convert into revenue during that year.
- Order-book uncertainty is a flagged risk: developing bespoke systems without finalised orders can pressure cash flows, mitigated by prioritising milestone-based agreements.

open.item: Goa facility construction was to start by Feb 15, 2025 but is delayed pending Goa government permission; company hopes to operationalize it before end of calendar year 2025.
Subsidiary ARI expected to add ~Rs 170 Crores top line for FY26 and become a 100% subsidiary by year-end (from current 76%).
Subsidiary UTS expected to add at least Rs 80 Crores to FY26 turnover, even excluding intercompany cross-transactions.
Subsidiaries expected to add ~Rs 250 Crores consolidated revenue for FY26 (ARI ~170 Cr + others ~80 Cr), at 35% EBITDA / 25% PAT benchmark.
FY26 capex guided at Rs 40-50 Crores, no significant capex planned.
Management expects meaningful new order inflow news in Q1FY27, not later than Q2FY27.

open.horizon: FY26 final dividend, payable after the 33rd AGM
open.item: The Board recommended a final dividend of ₹1 per equity share of ₹1 each (100% of face value) for FY26, subject to member approval at the 33rd AGM, with a record date of August 21, 2026.
Of the Rs 1336 Crores consolidated order book (Rs 1000 Cr ex-AMC), most is expected to convert to FY2027 revenue, with the bulk of deliveries in Q2 and Q3 FY2027.
Order book expected to touch around Rs 3000 Crores at some point during FY2027 to support ~Rs 2500 Crores of FY2028 execution as part of the Rs 4000 Cr cumulative plan.
UTS and ARI combined expected to generate ~Rs 365 Crores revenue in FY2027, at margins of ARI 27-30% and UTS ~30-31%.
Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle (150kg payload, combat/logistics/casualty evacuation) planned for commercial launch this financial year (FY2027).
HyperStrike interceptor drone production to start this financial year (FY2027), with initial capacity of 5000 units/shift/month, scalable to 15,000.
About ₹1,000 crore of the order book is expected to convert into revenue during FY27.
Commercial launch of the Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle is planned for FY27.
AI Turing associate company (Barbarik, Prahasta, hard-kill products) expected to make a meaningful contribution to overall revenue and profits by FY2027.
ARI's standalone PAT margin (~25% currently) expected to converge toward Zen's consolidated margin average once integration is complete, expected in FY2027.
FY2027 expected to record the highest turnover in company history, a 'very big year'.
Anti-drone tender sizes are increasing and expected to become very large specifically in FY2027.

Company must scale quarterly execution from current ~Rs 250-300 Crores/quarter run-rate to ~Rs 500 Crores/quarter (deemed achievable) and eventually ~Rs 750 Crores/quarter (deemed to require changes) to meet the FY28 cumulative target.
Significant US orders expected by FY2027 leveraging ARI's dealer network in Americas.
